rationale: Extensive assessment of electroretinographic profiles across both syndromic juvenile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (JNCL) and non-syndromic CLN3-associated retinal degeneration (RP101) confirms that full-field ERG at presentation demonstrates either an electronegative configuration (b-wave reduction out of proportion to a-wave preservation due to inner retinal/bipolar cell impairment) or generalized rod-cone pattern attenuation/extinction. No clinical studies in the literature report an isolated rod-specific dysfunction pattern in CLN3 retinopathy, strongly distinguishing it from classical rod-led retinitis pigmentosa.

evidence.text: In a retrospective series of five children with genetically confirmed CLN3 disease undergoing visual electrophysiology, electronegative ERGs were identified in 100% of tested individuals.

source.title: Early recognition of CLN3 disease facilitated by visual electrophysiology and multimodal imaging
source.quote: Electronegative ERGs were identified in all patients. Bull's eye maculopathies found in all patients.

evidence.text: Among eight children evaluated for juvenile Batten disease (CLN3), full-field ERG demonstrated an electronegative waveform in four patients (50%) and undetectable responses due to severe outer retinal degeneration in the remaining four patients (50%), with zero showing isolated rod dysfunction.

source.title: Juvenile Batten Disease (CLN3): Detailed Ocular Phenotype, Novel Observations, Delayed and Mistaken Diagnosis, and Recommendations for Clinical Management
source.quote: An electronegative ERG was present in 4 patients (50%), but with additional a-wave reduction, there was an undetectable ERG in the remaining 4 patients.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 10 patients with isolated, non-syndromic CLN3-associated retinal degeneration, full-field electroretinography demonstrated a generalized rod-cone pattern of dysfunction in 6 patients and undetectable responses in 2 patients, with none exhibiting isolated rod impairment.

source.title: Detailed Clinical Phenotype and Molecular Genetic Findings in CLN3-Associated Isolated Retinal Degeneration
source.quote: Electroretinography revealed a rod-cone pattern of dysfunction in 6 patients and were completely undetectable in 2 patients.

evidence.text: Electronegative ERG waveforms reflect post-phototransduction inner retinal dysfunction; variants in CLN3 are established genetic causes of negative ERGs and produce preferential inner retinal rod bipolar cell death prior to complete outer retinal photoreceptor loss.

source.title: Negative electroretinograms: genetic and acquired causes, diagnostic approaches and physiological insights

new_directions.question_text: What is the sensitivity and specificity of the DA bright-flash electronegative b/a ratio cutoff (<1.0) in separating early RP101 from early STGD1 and classical RP cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: STGD1 typically preserves peripheral rod ERG responses until late stages, while standard RP shows marked isolated rod a- and b-wave attenuation without b-wave predominance loss. Establishing precise diagnostic ROC curves for b/a amplitude ratios will allow rapid distinguishing of RP101 phenotypes.

new_directions.question_text: Does inner retinal bipolar cell rescue via targeted gene therapy prevent progression to non-recordable ERG in non-syndromic CLN3 human retinal organoid models?
new_directions.rationale: Evidence indicates the negative ERG in CLN3 is driven by early bipolar cell vulnerability, suggesting inner retinal therapy could preserve outer retinal architecture and visual function.
